IT New Hire Technology Overview

Let's set up your Nsight Mac.

Welcome to Nsight Health. This takes 11 steps and about an hour, and most of that is waiting. IT also goes through all of it with you on Day 1.

Start here
  • 1 USB-C cable
  • 2 Receiver
  • 3 Internet cable

Every plug has a number. Match the number on the plug to the number on the port.

Before you start, have these nearby

Do one step at a time. When you finish a step, click Done and the next one opens. Stuck? Click Get help any time.

Get help

Hardware

2 steps, about 7 minutes. Plug everything in first. Skip anything you didn't pick in your new-hire questionnaire.

Didn't pick a monitor? Just plug in your Mac's power cable (the magnetic end snaps into the long port), then click Done.
  1. Put your Mac on the stand.
  2. Plug the monitor's power cable into the wall and the monitor. Press the monitor's power button.
  3. Plug the USB-C cable into 1 on the back of the monitor (the small oval port).
  4. Plug the other end into 1 on your Mac (either small oval port on the left side). 1 goes to 1!
  5. Plug in your Mac's power cable. The magnetic end snaps into the long port.
Heads up: Leave the HDMI cable and the Anker hub in the box. They're a backup in case the monitor doesn't work.
Monitor stays black? See the fix
  1. Plug one end of an internet (Ethernet) cable into any numbered port (1–4) on your home router. Not the one marked Internet or WAN.
  2. Plug the other end into 3 on the back of the monitor (the square port). Push until it clicks.
  3. That's it. Your Mac now uses the cable for internet.
Heads up: This only works when your Mac is connected to the monitor with the USB-C cable. Router too far away, or no monitor? Use Wi-Fi for now (you'll connect in Step 3) and tell IT.
Training calls freeze when Wi-Fi drops. A cable stops that, so it's worth it.

Software

9 steps. Your Mac walks you through the rest.

  1. Open your Mac's lid. It turns on by itself. If not, press the power button (top-right key).
  2. On the Wi-Fi screen, pick your Wi-Fi and type its password. (Using the internet cable? This one screen may not show up. That's OK, keep going.)
  3. Click Get Started.
  4. Click Continue through language, country and accessibility.
  5. Choose Set up as new.
  6. On the Remote Management screen, click Enroll.
Heads up: If it asks for an Apple ID, skip it. Don't use your personal one.
Use your Mac's own keyboard and trackpad for now. Your Logitech keyboard and mouse get set up in Step 7.
Wi-Fi won't connect? See the fix
  1. Type your @nsightcare.com email.
  2. Type the temporary password from your welcome email.
  3. Click I understand.
  4. Make a new password. Pick one you'll remember.
  5. Click Enroll, pick your time zone, then click Continue.
  6. Sign in again with your new password.
Heads up: The screen may go blank for a moment. That's normal. Just wait.
  1. Click Create a new account. You'll click it twice.
  2. When FileVault asks, click Enable now. (FileVault keeps your data locked and safe.)
  3. Wait while “Setting up your Mac” runs. This takes about 15 minutes.
  4. When you see Setup complete, close that window.
Heads up: Don't close the setup window or shut the lid while it's working.
  1. A Google Drive window opens. Click Get started, then Sign in.
  2. Chrome may show a warning or not load. This is expected. Close it.
  3. Click the Apple icon (top-left corner), then Restart, then Restart again.
  4. Sign back in with the first part of your email (everything before the @). Example: jdoe
  5. If a Logi Bluetooth pop-up shows up, click Allow.
Heads up: Errors in this step are normal. The restart fixes them.
Didn't pick a keyboard and mouse? Skip this step. Just click Done.
  1. Find the tiny USB receiver. It's tucked into the side of the keyboard box. Don't throw the box away until you have it!
  2. Plug the receiver into 2 on the back of the monitor (the rectangular USB port).
  3. Pull out the plastic tabs from the mouse and keyboard. This turns the batteries on. If you see an on/off switch, turn it on.
  4. Flip the keyboard over. A green light is blinking. That means it's ready to connect.
  5. On your Mac, click the Apple icon (top-left corner), then System Settings, then Bluetooth.
  6. Find your Logitech keyboard in the list and click Connect.
  7. If your Mac shows a number, type it on the Logitech keyboard and press Enter.
Heads up: The keyboard won't connect by itself. It only works after you click Connect in Bluetooth settings.
Test it: type a few letters. If they show up, you're done!
Keyboard or mouse not working? See the fix
  1. When asked, make Chrome your default browser and click OK.
  2. In Google Drive, click Get started and sign in with your Nsight email.
  3. In Chrome, click Continue as your Nsight account.
  4. You'll see “This profile will be managed.” That's normal. Click Continue.
  5. Choose Continue to work in this profile, then click Confirm.
  6. When asked to install Google Drive, click Sign in.
  7. Click Action required in Chrome, then Enable extension.
Heads up: Work tools won't open in Safari. Always use Chrome.
Seeing “access denied”? See the fix
Before you start: On your phone, install Google Authenticator: iPhone · Android
  1. In Chrome, click your profile picture (top-right), then Manage your Google Account.
  2. Click Security & sign-in, then 2-Step Verification.
  3. Click Authenticator, then Set up authenticator. A QR code appears.
  4. In the app on your phone, tap the colorful +, then Scan a QR code. Point your camera at the screen.
  5. Click Next. Type the 6-digit code from your phone, then click Verify.
  6. Click Turn on. Done!
Heads up: The code changes every 30 seconds, so always use the newest one. You'll need your phone every time you sign in. Keep it with you.
  1. Open Slack from your Dock. (Not there? Open Finder, then Applications, then Slack.)
  2. Click Sign in to Slack, then Google.
  3. Pick your Nsight account and click Continue.
  4. Join Nsight. It's the one with the blue logo (the bigger group).
  5. Click Sign in with Google, then Continue, then Open Slack app.
You're in! Say hi in #general. Need IT? Message #ask-it.
Slack says “access denied”? See the fix
  1. In Gmail, open the 1Password invite and click Activate your account.
  2. Type your name and click Next.
  3. Make a strong password: 3 or 4 random words plus a few numbers. Long, but easy to remember.
  4. Click Generate Secret Key, then Save PDF. Keep this file safe and don't delete it.
  5. Click Next. Check that the 1Password icon is pinned in Chrome. (Don't see it? Contact IT.)
Heads up: Don't write your password down. If you forget it, IT can reset it.
Locked out of 1Password later? See the fix

You're all set

On Day 1, join the Google Meet link in your calendar at 9 AM EST on your first Monday. IT will go through everything with you, whether you did these steps or not.

Something not working?

Click your problem to see the fix.

My screen doesn't match the pictures

Screens change sometimes, so yours may look a little different.

  1. Look for the bold button words from the step.
  2. Don't see them? Stop. Don't guess.
  3. Take a photo of your screen with your phone and contact IT.

IT goes through all of this with you on Day 1 too.

My Mac or monitor won't turn on

Mac won't turn on: plug in its power cable and wait 5 minutes (the battery may be empty). Then press and hold the power button (top-right key) for 3 seconds.

Monitor stays black:

  1. Is the monitor plugged into the wall and turned on?
  2. Push both ends of the USB-C cable in all the way.
  3. Try the other oval port on your Mac.
  4. Keep the Mac's lid open.

Backup plan: plug the Anker hub into your Mac. Then connect the HDMI cable from the hub to the monitor's HDMI port. Plug the keyboard receiver into the hub too.

My keyboard or mouse doesn't work
  1. Keyboard: flip it over. Is a green light blinking? It's waiting to connect. Follow Step 7 to connect it with Bluetooth.
  2. Mouse: is the tiny USB receiver plugged into the back of the monitor? Can't find it? Check the side of the keyboard box.
  3. Did you pull out the plastic battery tabs and turn on any on/off switch?
  4. Still nothing? Use the Mac's own keyboard and trackpad for now and contact IT.
My internet keeps dropping

Try these, in order:

  1. Best fix: use an internet cable. See Step 2.
  2. Move closer to your router.
  3. Restart your router: unplug it, wait 30 seconds, plug it back in.
  4. Backup: turn on your phone's hotspot and connect your Mac to it.

Missing training because of it? Tell your manager or trainer right away.

I'm locked out of 1Password

Don't create a new account. IT can get you back in.

  1. Lost your Secret Key? Check your Downloads folder for a PDF called 1Password Emergency Kit.
  2. Forgot your password, or still stuck? Contact IT and say “1Password reset”. IT will email you a link to set a new password.
Slack or Google says “access denied”

Some Nsight tools only work on your Nsight Mac. This keeps company data safe. Check:

  1. You're on your Nsight Mac, not a personal computer.
  2. You're using Chrome, not Safari.
  3. Chrome shows your Nsight name in the top-right corner.

Still denied? Take a photo of the message and contact IT.
